The access workflow for Harborlight Tool Library is designed to ensure that tools are used safely and efficiently. Tools are categorized and labeled with the amber intake label to indicate they are ready for use. This label helps staff quickly identify tools that are available for immediate lending. Each tool is checked out through a digital system that records the borrower's name, the date of borrowing, and the date of return. This system also tracks high-risk tools, which require additional safety measures.

Volunteer handover at Harborlight Tool Library is crucial for maintaining a smooth workflow. Volunteers are trained to handle tools with care and are provided with a checklist to ensure all tools are returned in good condition. Upon returning tools, volunteers must report any damage or issues to the library staff. Additionally, volunteers are encouraged to provide feedback on the usability of the tools and the library's policies, which helps in continuous improvement. The maintenance of Harborlight Tool Library is essential to ensure that tools remain safe and functional.

Regular inspections are conducted to check for wear and tear, and tools are replaced or repaired as needed. High-risk tools undergo a thorough test by two people to ensure they meet safety standards before being returned to service. Maintenance schedules are integrated into the library's operational plan, ensuring that all tools are maintained according to safety guidelines. Safety is paramount at Harborlight Tool Library. Every high-risk tool requires a safety review, which is conducted by two people every Wednesday.

This review includes a comprehensive test of the tool to ensure it meets safety standards. Safety training is provided to all staff and volunteers to ensure they are knowledgeable about the safe use of tools. Regular safety audits are also conducted to identify and address any potential hazards or areas for improvement in the library's safety protocols. This implementation brief outlines the key aspects of the Harborlight Tool Library, ensuring that tools are used safely, maintained properly, and that all safety protocols are followed.

The monthly maintenance calendar for Harborlight Tool Library includes regular inspections of all tools, which are conducted every two weeks. Tools are checked for wear and tear, and any issues are addressed promptly.

High-risk tools undergo a thorough test by two people every Wednesday, as mentioned earlier. This test includes a series of safety checks to ensure the tool is safe for use.

For example, if a high-risk tool is a chainsaw, the two-person test would involve checking the blade for sharp edges, testing the chain for proper tension, and ensuring the safety lock is functioning correctly.

This ensures that the chainsaw is safe to use and meets all safety standards before being returned to service.

The safety reviews for Harborlight Tool Library have been moved from every Wednesday to every Friday. This change ensures that tools are reviewed promptly and that safety protocols are followed regularly.

The intake label for tools has been changed from amber to teal. This change helps staff quickly identify tools that are ready for use, making the process more efficient.
